title: Uber Holiday Redesign
subtitle: Ride-hailing App
summary: A holiday-season redesign of the Uber app for class, adding Party Pass, group gatherings, airport pickups with miles, and gifting.
role: UX/UI designer (style guide, user flow, hi-fi screens)

overview.heading: Holiday rides are group plans, not solo trips.
overview.body: Over the holidays, one person often ends up getting everyone else home or to the table. This class project (AMDE 447) redesigns Uber around that: a host can fund rides for party guests, coordinate pickups for a gathering, and handle airport arrivals, without a group chat holding it all together.

process.label: User flow
process.text: Party Pass: the host sets a ride budget and shares a code, and guests scan it to request rides the host can track. If the pass has expired, the host can reopen or close it. If a fare is over budget, they can raise the budget or book a shared ride with another guest.

process.label: User flow
process.text: Holiday gathering: the host sets a destination and arrive-by time, adds guests and pickups, and a smart schedule checks for delays like a late flight before re-planning. Then the host either pays or splits the cost with people sharing a car, confirms, and tracks every ride.

process.label: Welcome motion
process.text: A seasonal launch screen: the Uber wordmark over a night sky with falling snow, and Santa's sleigh kicking up powder across the hills.

process.label: Gathering
process.text: The host's view of Monica's Thanksgiving: party name, location, and a guest list with a status pill for each person, from Checked in to Needs check-in to At Home.

process.label: Expired deal
process.text: When HOLIDAY20 has expired, the rider gets a clear warning and a list of deals that still apply. The ones that don't fit this ride are greyed out with the reason, and paying the regular fare is always an option.

process.label: Airport pickup
process.text: The last, optional step of an airport pickup: pick an airline program, enter a member number, and see an estimate of the miles this ride will earn. Skip for now stays visible.

decision.title: Every dead end gets a way out.
decision.body: Holiday plans break: codes expire, fares go over budget, flights land late. I mapped each of those as a recovery path in the flows first, so the screens always offer the next move, like reopening a pass, sharing a ride, re-planning a pickup or picking another deal, instead of just showing an error.

outcome: A style guide, two FigJam user flows for Party Pass and holiday gatherings, and high-fidelity Figma screens for the welcome motion, gathering, deals and airport pickup.
